title: Vectorized Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of vectorized operations and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply arithmetic on vectors in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.

content.intro: Vectorized Operations is part of Operators, Vectors, and Vectorized Computing. Start with arithmetic on vectors and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: R works naturally with vectors, so indexing and vectorized operations can transform many values without a manual loop.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: R works naturally with vectors, so indexing and vectorized operations can transform many values without a manual loop. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Predict the output length and selected positions, then test a value on the condition boundary. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.

content_blocks.limitations: The logical index keeps values above a visible threshold; check the boundary and result length. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For vectorized operations, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
